correctness.rationale: Left-associated products of natural basis vectors select coefficients along an index walk, so the right power at r is nonzero iff a length-(r−1) walk has nonzero product. Reduction preserves elementwise nilness. Independently, if the residue digraph has a directed cycle, a shortest cycle has no extra arcs on its vertex set; the sum of its basis vectors never has a zero left-associated power, as multiplication by that sum updates its cycle coordinates cyclically by nonzero coefficients. Conversely, acyclicity bounds a unit run by n−1, so a walk with t nonunit edges has length at most n(t+1)−1. A length-ns walk therefore has zero product. At length ns−1 a nonzero product forces s−1 valuation-one breaks and s Hamiltonian unit runs in the unique forced topological order. Each break is the same return entry, and its (s−1)-fold product times units is nonzero; when s=1 there are no breaks, and at n=1 the return is diagonal. Clauses 2–3 are on the finite-index (nil-table) domain of ν; a Hamiltonian path in a cyclic residue graph does not suffice. Source inclusion–exclusion counts residue DAGs, every residue has q^(s−1) lifts, and the unique Hamiltonian order avoids overcounting: n−1 unit entries, one valuation-one return when s≥2, freely chosen other forward entries and nonunit backward/diagonal entries give the stated exponents. An independently written exhaustive rank-two Z/4 check verified 48 nil and 16 index-five tables among 256, checking principal powers and right-power submodules directly. value.rationale: Keeping the residue support fixed can hide all nonunit information. The classification identifies exactly the one return entry and valuation needed for the longest nonzero right powers, and counts how frequently this extremal behavior occurs in labelled lifts across finite chain rings. This supplies a meaningful sharp boundary and an exact census without conflating ordinary and right nilindices or isomorphism classes.
